facts.statement: Orodromeus is a small, herbivorous dinosaur belonging to the family Thescelosauridae that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Orodromeus (meaning "Mountain Runner") is a genus of herbivorous orodromine thescelosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America.

facts.statement: The genus name Orodromeus means "Mountain Runner" and refers to the animal's cursorial (running) habits and the Egg Mountain discovery site.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek ὄρος, oros, "mountain", in reference to the Egg Mountain site, and δρομεύς, dromeus, "runner", referring to the cursorial habits of the animal.

facts.statement: Fossils of Orodromeus were discovered by Robert Makela in Teton County, Montana, while excavating a nesting colony of Maiasaura.
facts.quote: The remains of Orodromeus were discovered by Robert Makela during the excavation in Teton County, Montana, of the Egg Mountain brooding colony of a much larger relative, Maiasaura.

facts.statement: The species Orodromeus makelai was named and described by Jack Horner and David B. Weishampel in 1988.
facts.quote: The type species, Orodromeus makelai, was named and shortly described by Jack Horner and David B. Weishampel in 1988.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Campanian stage of the Two Medicine Formation, approximately 75 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MOR 294, was found in a layer of the Two Medicine Formation, dating from the Campanian stage, about 75 million years ago.

facts.statement: Some eggs originally attributed to Orodromeus are now believed to belong to a troodontid dinosaur, possibly Stenonychosaurus.
facts.quote: However, MOR 246 and other eggs from Egg Mountain are now considered to belong to a troodontid which may be Stenonychosaurus.

facts.statement: Horner and Weishampel estimated the length of Orodromeus to be 2.5 meters.
facts.quote: Its length was estimated by Horner & Weishampel at 2.5 metres.

facts.statement: Modern classification views Orodromeus as a basal member of the Euornithopoda, as the group Hypsilophodontidae is considered unnatural and paraphyletic.
facts.quote: Today these are seen as an unnatural, paraphyletic, group, and Orodromeus is simply considered to be a basal member of the Euornithopoda.

facts.statement: Brown et al. (2013) classified Orodromeus in the family Thescelosauridae and named the subfamily Orodrominae after it.
facts.quote: Brown et al. (2013) put it in the family Thescelosauridae and named a new subfamily (Orodrominae) after it.

facts.statement: Jack Horner concluded that Orodromeus young were precocial based on the advanced development of their bones and teeth.
facts.quote: Because of the advanced development of the bones and teeth of the embryos, Horner concluded that the young of Orodromeus were precocial.

facts.statement: Researchers speculate that Orodromeus may have burrowed, similar to its relative Oryctodromeus, based on the unusual packing of its fossil bones.
facts.quote: It has been speculated that this animal may have burrowed much like its relative Oryctodromeus, based upon the packing of their bones in situations where they typically would have been scattered.

facts.statement: Ten nests of Orodromeus have been found, containing eggs arranged in a spiral pattern.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado 10 nidos de Orodromeus, con huevos dispuestos en forma espiral.

facts.statement: The unhatched eggshells were not trampled, indicating that the young abandoned the nest immediately upon hatching.
facts.quote: Los cascarones no estaban pisoteados lo que muestra que los pequeños abandonaron el nido al nacer.

facts.statement: CT scans of unhatched Orodromeus eggs showed well-developed embryos, unlike those of Maiasaura which hatched helpless.
facts.quote: Una tomografía axial computada de huevos sin eclosionar, mostró que los embriones estaban bien desarrollados, a diferencia de los del Maiasauria, los cuales nacían indefensos.

facts.statement: Orodromeus nested in large colonies where individual nests were excavated and covered to better control temperature.
facts.quote: Orodromeus anidaba en grandes colonias donde cada nido individual era excavado y cubierto para una mayor control de la temperatura.

facts.statement: It appears that Orodromeus parents cared for their nests by driving away small predators.
facts.quote: Al parecer los padres cuidaban de los nidos, alejando a pequeños depredadores.

facts.statement: Orodromeus apparently possessed a strong jugal bone similar to that of Zephyrosaurus.
facts.quote: Aparentemente tenía un yugal fuerte similar al de Zephyrosaurus.

facts.statement: The specific name makelai honors Robert Makela, who died in a car accident shortly after discovering the fossils.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honró al difunto Makela.

facts.statement: In 1990, Laosaurus minimus was considered a second species of Orodromeus, though this assignment remains uncertain due to fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: En 1990, la especie Laosaurus minimus, descrita por Charles Gilmore en 1909 basada en NMC 9438, un miembro posterior izquierdo parcial y piezas de vértebra de la Formación Allison en Alberta, se consideró como la segunda especie de Orodromeus.

facts.statement: This small herbivore likely coexisted with dinosaurs such as Daspletosaurus and Einiosaurus.
facts.quote: Este pequeño herbívoro probablemente coexistió con dinosaurios como Daspletosaurus y Einiosaurus.

facts.statement: Several Orodromeus nests were found alongside those of Maiasaura.
facts.quote: Se concen varios nidos que fueron encontrados junto a los de Maiasaura.

facts.statement: Orodromeus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
